name: Redis
description: An in-memory store for caches, queues and sessions, reachable only by other containers on this host. The official image takes no password from the environment, so it runs without one.

access.note: This Redis has no password. The official image takes requirepass only from a command argument or a configuration file, neither of which can carry a secret generated here, so nothing authenticates. Its port is never published to the host, so the exposure is every other container on the same Docker network: treat the store as readable, writable and erasable by all of them.

inputs.name: maxmemory
inputs.label: Container memory limit
inputs.description: The container's limit. Redis is not given a maxmemory of its own, so it keeps allocating until this cap stops it.

ports.name: redis
ports.purpose: Client connections from other containers on this host

volumes.name: data
volumes.purpose: The RDB snapshot Redis restores from

update.notes: Redis 8 reads the RDB snapshot written by Redis 7 and is not reversible; back up the volume first. Redis 8 also autoloads its four bundled modules, so baseline memory is higher than Redis 7's.
